A hydrate is a distinct substance containing the anhydrous form, not a specialization of it. closeMatch claims similarity without subsumption. The ontology_id and the record's own identifier are unchanged.

identifier CHEBI:35458 -> kgmicrobe.compound:cecl3_x_7_h2o; mapping_quality EXACT_MATCH -> NARROW_MATCH. The record is a hydrate of CHEBI:35458 ('cerium trichloride') and was sharing that term's identifier — the identity collapse MAPPING_SEMANTICS §3 forbids, which made a distinct substance indistinguishable from its anhydrous parent downstream. ChEBI has no term for this hydrate and the record carries no verified CAS, so steps 1 and 2 are unavailable and step 3 applies.

molecular_formula 'CeCl3' -> 'CeCl3.7H2O'. The recorded value described the anhydrous salt while the label names a hydrate, understating the mass by 18 g/mol per water. Corrected because the label states 7 water(s) of hydration, and the recorded formula was byte-identical to the anhydrous parent CHEBI:35458's ChEBI formula ('CeCl3') — the mark of a value inherited from the parent rather than measured for this record. Water appended in ChEBI's own dot-separated notation.

mapping_quality NARROW_MATCH -> CLOSE_MATCH, predicate skos:narrowMatch -> skos:closeMatch. narrowMatch asserts this record is *narrower in meaning* than CHEBI:35458 ('cerium trichloride') — a subsumption ChEBI itself denies: it files hydrates under CHEBI:35505 'hydrate', never under the anhydrous compound, which is not an ancestor even transitively. A hydrate is a distinct substance containing the anhydrous form, not a specialization of it. closeMatch claims similarity without subsumption. The ontology_id and the record's own identifier are unchanged.

Four current source recipes and MediaDive1444 name CeCl3·7H2O. Independent supplier/PubChem agree on specific CAS18618-55-8 and formula. The complete ignored-inclusive neighbor scan found no other current owner of this CAS. No eligible exact CHEBI/NCIT term was established by the bounded current CAS/name queries. Promote local primary to cas:18618-55-8, preserve the old local registry identity, and broadMatch CHEBI35458. Existing CeCl3.7H2O matches. Add evidenced CAS only; do not automatically copy a PubChem structure/CID. Primary source references: https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/US/en/product/aldrich/228931; https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/rest/pug/substance/sourceid/Sigma-Aldrich/228931_ALDRICH/JSON; https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/rest/pug/compound/name/18618-55-8/property/Title,MolecularFormula,MolecularWeight,InChI,InChIKey,CanonicalSMILES/JSON; https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chebi/backend/api/public/compound/35458/. evidence.notes: [HISTORICAL — superseded by the #321 re-grade below: this record is a hydrate of CHEBI:78036, not an exact match to it] Imported from CultureMech pipeline, quality=DIRECT_MATCH

identifier CHEBI:78036 -> kgmicrobe.compound:cu_no32_x_3_h2o; mapping_quality EXACT_MATCH -> NARROW_MATCH. The record is a hydrate of CHEBI:78036 ('copper(II) nitrate') and was sharing that term's identifier — the identity collapse MAPPING_SEMANTICS §3 forbids, which made a distinct substance indistinguishable from its anhydrous parent downstream. ChEBI has no term for this hydrate and the record carries no verified CAS, so steps 1 and 2 are unavailable and step 3 applies.

molecular_formula 'Cu.2NO3' -> 'Cu.2NO3.3H2O'. The recorded value described the anhydrous salt while the label names a hydrate, understating the mass by 18 g/mol per water. Corrected because the label states 3 water(s) of hydration, and the recorded formula was byte-identical to the anhydrous parent CHEBI:78036's ChEBI formula ('Cu.2NO3') — the mark of a value inherited from the parent rather than measured for this record. Water appended in ChEBI's own dot-separated notation.

mapping_quality NARROW_MATCH -> CLOSE_MATCH, predicate skos:narrowMatch -> skos:closeMatch. narrowMatch asserts this record is *narrower in meaning* than CHEBI:78036 ('copper(II) nitrate') — a subsumption ChEBI itself denies: it files hydrates under CHEBI:35505 'hydrate', never under the anhydrous compound, which is not an ancestor even transitively. A hydrate is a distinct substance containing the anhydrous form, not a specialization of it. closeMatch claims similarity without subsumption. The ontology_id and the record's own identifier are unchanged.

Historical source, current formula and independent GSRS/PubChem agree on copper(II) nitrate trihydrate CAS10031-43-3. The ignored-inclusive owner scan found no other current owner of this CAS. Promote local primary to cas:10031-43-3, retain existing local registry identity, and NARROW_MATCH/broadMatch CHEBI78036. No exact eligible CHEBI/NCIT trihydrate term was established by the bounded queries. Keep CAS and Cu.2NO3.3H2O. Do not automatically add CID/SMILES/InChI from the reviewed comparator. Primary source references: https://gsrs.ncats.nih.gov/api/v1/substances/066PG1506T?view=full; https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/rest/pug/compound/name/10031-43-3/property/Title,MolecularFormula,MolecularWeight,InChI,InChIKey,CanonicalSMILES/JSON; https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chebi/backend/api/public/compound/78036/. Captures, exact input hashes and scope limits: reports/step7d_mapping_901_20261103/evidence-manifest.json. Independent review identifies the existing exact synonym 'copper(2+) dinitrate' as the water-free parent, not this hydrate; preserve it as REJECTED_LABEL. This curation adds no scientific, mapping-release or role approval; changed owner bytes withdraw inherited support.

identifier CHEBI:91259 -> kgmicrobe.compound:na2hpo4_x_12_h2o; mapping_quality EXACT_MATCH -> NARROW_MATCH. The record is a hydrate of CHEBI:91259 ('disodium hydrogenphosphate dodecahydrate') and was sharing that term's identifier — the identity collapse MAPPING_SEMANTICS §3 forbids, which made a distinct substance indistinguishable from its anhydrous parent downstream. ChEBI has no term for this hydrate and the record carries no verified CAS, so steps 1 and 2 are unavailable and step 3 applies.

molecular_formula 'HO4P.2Na' -> '12H2O.HO4P.2Na'. The recorded value described the anhydrous salt while the label names a hydrate, understating the mass by 18 g/mol per water. Corrected because adopted verbatim from the mapped term CHEBI:91259 ('disodium hydrogenphosphate dodecahydrate'), which is the specific hydrate and already carries the water.

mapping_quality NARROW_MATCH -> CLOSE_MATCH, predicate skos:narrowMatch -> skos:closeMatch. narrowMatch asserts this record is *narrower in meaning* than CHEBI:91259 ('disodium hydrogenphosphate dodecahydrate') — a subsumption ChEBI itself denies: it files hydrates under CHEBI:35505 'hydrate', never under the anhydrous compound, which is not an ancestor even transitively. A hydrate is a distinct substance containing the anhydrous form, not a specialization of it. closeMatch claims similarity without subsumption. The ontology_id and the record's own identifier are unchanged.

evidence.notes: MediaDive REST gives CAS 13446-18-9 = magnesium nitrate hexahydrate for source name 'Mg(NO3)2 x 6 H2O'. CHEBI has only the anhydrous parent (CHEBI:64736 'magnesium nitrate'), so the hexahydrate is a narrowMatch to it, with cas:13446-18-9 preserved as the exact-identity primary (cf. ammonium molybdate tetrahydrate).
Parent anhydrous term CHEBI:64736 'magnesium nitrate'; no hexahydrate term exists in CHEBI.

mapping_quality NARROW_MATCH -> CLOSE_MATCH, predicate skos:narrowMatch -> skos:closeMatch. narrowMatch asserts this record is *narrower in meaning* than CHEBI:64736 ('magnesium nitrate') — a subsumption ChEBI itself denies: it files hydrates under CHEBI:35505 'hydrate', never under the anhydrous compound, which is not an ancestor even transitively. A hydrate is a distinct substance containing the anhydrous form, not a specialization of it. closeMatch claims similarity without subsumption. The ontology_id and the record's own identifier are unchanged.

MediaDiveingredient1763 explicitly names Mg(NO3)2 x6H2O and CAS13446-18-9; freshPubChemCAS resolvesCID202877 with magnesium dinitrate hexahydrate/H12MgN2O12. ParentCHEBI64736 is magnesium nitrate withoutwaters. No exacteligiblehydrate candidatefound. RetainformCAS and broadMatch toparent with B1registry; no inventedchemicalprops. See the complete identity, mapping, chemistry and synonym assessment in reports/step7d_mapping_901_20261103/authors/science-b/full-assessments.json; owner selector data/ingredients/mapped/Magnesium_Nitrate_Hexahydrate.yaml. Primary source references: https://github.com/CultureBotAI/CultureBotHT; https://mediadive.dsmz.de/rest/ingredients; https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/rest/pug/compound/name/13446-18-9/property/MolecularFormula,MolecularWeight,InChI,InChIKey,IUPACName/JSON; https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chebi/backend/api/public/compound/64736/. Captures, exact input hashes and scope limits: reports/step7d_mapping_901_20261103/evidence-manifest.json. evidence.notes: [HISTORICAL — superseded by the #321 re-grade below: this record is a hydrate of CHEBI:34887, not an exact match to it] Imported from CultureMech pipeline, quality=DIRECT_MATCH

identifier CHEBI:34887 -> kgmicrobe.compound:nicl2_x_2_h2o; mapping_quality EXACT_MATCH -> NARROW_MATCH. The record is a hydrate of CHEBI:34887 ('nickel dichloride') and was sharing that term's identifier — the identity collapse MAPPING_SEMANTICS §3 forbids, which made a distinct substance indistinguishable from its anhydrous parent downstream. ChEBI has no term for this hydrate and the record carries no verified CAS, so steps 1 and 2 are unavailable and step 3 applies.

molecular_formula 'Cl2Ni' -> 'Cl2Ni.2H2O'. The recorded value described the anhydrous salt while the label names a hydrate, understating the mass by 18 g/mol per water. Corrected because the label states 2 water(s) of hydration, and the recorded formula was byte-identical to the anhydrous parent CHEBI:34887's ChEBI formula ('Cl2Ni') — the mark of a value inherited from the parent rather than measured for this record. Water appended in ChEBI's own dot-separated notation.

mapping_quality NARROW_MATCH -> CLOSE_MATCH, predicate skos:narrowMatch -> skos:closeMatch. narrowMatch asserts this record is *narrower in meaning* than CHEBI:34887 ('nickel dichloride') — a subsumption ChEBI itself denies: it files hydrates under CHEBI:35505 'hydrate', never under the anhydrous compound, which is not an ancestor even transitively. A hydrate is a distinct substance containing the anhydrous form, not a specialization of it. closeMatch claims similarity without subsumption. The ontology_id and the record's own identifier are unchanged.

Preserve the local dihydrate identity. MediaDive981 explicitly names NiCl2 x2H2O; primary experimental literature establishes nickel chloride dihydrate. Its automatic CAS7718-54-9 belongs to the water-free parent and is not adopted. See the complete identity, mapping, chemistry and synonym assessment in reports/step7d_mapping_901_20261103/authors/science-c/assessments-v2.json; owner selector data/ingredients/mapped/Nicl2_X_2_H2o.yaml. Primary source references: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chebi/backend/api/public/compound/34887/; https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/api/search?q=NiCl2%20x%202%20H2O&ontology=chebi,ncit&rows=100; https://bacmedia.dsmz.de/ingredients/981; https://ojs.uel.br/revistas/uel/index.php/semexatas/article/download/2681/2331/8885; https://journals.iucr.org/q/issues/1967/10/00/. Captures, exact input hashes and scope limits: reports/step7d_mapping_901_20261103/evidence-manifest.json. This curation adds no scientific, mapping-release or role approval; changed owner bytes withdraw inherited support.

evidence.notes: [HISTORICAL — superseded by the #321 re-grade below: this record is a hydrate of CHEBI:34887, not an exact match to it] Imported from CultureMech pipeline, quality=DIRECT_MATCH

identifier CHEBI:34887 -> kgmicrobe.compound:nicl2_x_2_h2o; mapping_quality EXACT_MATCH -> NARROW_MATCH. The record is a hydrate of CHEBI:34887 ('nickel dichloride') and was sharing that term's identifier — the identity collapse MAPPING_SEMANTICS §3 forbids, which made a distinct substance indistinguishable from its anhydrous parent downstream. ChEBI has no term for this hydrate and the record carries no verified CAS, so steps 1 and 2 are unavailable and step 3 applies.

molecular_formula 'Cl2Ni' -> 'Cl2Ni.2H2O'. The recorded value described the anhydrous salt while the label names a hydrate, understating the mass by 18 g/mol per water. Corrected because the label states 2 water(s) of hydration, and the recorded formula was byte-identical to the anhydrous parent CHEBI:34887's ChEBI formula ('Cl2Ni') — the mark of a value inherited from the parent rather than measured for this record. Water appended in ChEBI's own dot-separated notation.

mapping_quality NARROW_MATCH -> CLOSE_MATCH, predicate skos:narrowMatch -> skos:closeMatch. narrowMatch asserts this record is *narrower in meaning* than CHEBI:34887 ('nickel dichloride') — a subsumption ChEBI itself denies: it files hydrates under CHEBI:35505 'hydrate', never under the anhydrous compound, which is not an ancestor even transitively. A hydrate is a distinct substance containing the anhydrous form, not a specialization of it. closeMatch claims similarity without subsumption. The ontology_id and the record's own identifier are unchanged.

Preserve the local dihydrate identity. MediaDive981 explicitly names NiCl2 x2H2O; primary experimental literature establishes nickel chloride dihydrate. Its automatic CAS7718-54-9 belongs to the water-free parent and is not adopted. See the complete identity, mapping, chemistry and synonym assessment in reports/step7d_mapping_901_20261103/authors/science-c/assessments-v2.json; owner selector data/ingredients/mapped/Nicl2_X_2_H2o.yaml. Primary source references: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chebi/backend/api/public/compound/34887/; https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/api/search?q=NiCl2%20x%202%20H2O&ontology=chebi,ncit&rows=100; https://bacmedia.dsmz.de/ingredients/981; https://ojs.uel.br/revistas/uel/index.php/semexatas/article/download/2681/2331/8885; https://journals.iucr.org/q/issues/1967/10/00/. Captures, exact input hashes and scope limits: reports/step7d_mapping_901_20261103/evidence-manifest.json. This curation adds no scientific, mapping-release or role approval; changed owner bytes withdraw inherited support.

The record is a hydrate of CHEBI:17750 ('glycine betaine') and was sharing that term's identifier — the identity collapse MAPPING_SEMANTICS §3 forbids, which made a distinct substance indistinguishable from its anhydrous parent downstream. ChEBI has no term for this hydrate and the record carries no verified CAS, so steps 1 and 2 are unavailable and step 3 applies.

molecular_formula 'C5H11NO2' -> 'C5H11NO2.H2O'. The recorded value described the anhydrous salt while the label names a hydrate, understating the mass by 18 g/mol per water. Corrected because the label states 1 water(s) of hydration, and the recorded formula was byte-identical to the anhydrous parent CHEBI:17750's ChEBI formula ('C5H11NO2') — the mark of a value inherited from the parent rather than measured for this record. Water appended in ChEBI's own dot-separated notation.

mapping_quality NARROW_MATCH -> CLOSE_MATCH, predicate skos:narrowMatch -> skos:closeMatch. narrowMatch asserts this record is *narrower in meaning* than CHEBI:17750 ('glycine betaine') — a subsumption ChEBI itself denies: it files hydrates under CHEBI:35505 'hydrate', never under the anhydrous compound, which is not an ancestor even transitively. A hydrate is a distinct substance containing the anhydrous form, not a specialization of it. closeMatch claims similarity without subsumption. The ontology_id and the record's own identifier are unchanged.

evidence.notes: [HISTORICAL — superseded by the #321 re-grade below: this record is a hydrate of CHEBI:37585, not an exact match to it] Imported from CultureMech pipeline, quality=DIRECT_MATCH

identifier CHEBI:37585 -> kgmicrobe.compound:nah2po4_x_2_h2o; mapping_quality SYNONYM_MATCH -> NARROW_MATCH. The record is a hydrate of CHEBI:37585 ('sodium dihydrogenphosphate') and was sharing that term's identifier — the identity collapse MAPPING_SEMANTICS §3 forbids, which made a distinct substance indistinguishable from its anhydrous parent downstream. ChEBI has no term for this hydrate and the record carries no verified CAS, so steps 1 and 2 are unavailable and step 3 applies.

molecular_formula 'H2O4P.Na' -> 'H2O4P.Na.2H2O'. The recorded value described the anhydrous salt while the label names a hydrate, understating the mass by 18 g/mol per water. Corrected because the label states 2 water(s) of hydration, and the recorded formula was byte-identical to the anhydrous parent CHEBI:37585's ChEBI formula ('H2O4P.Na') — the mark of a value inherited from the parent rather than measured for this record. Water appended in ChEBI's own dot-separated notation.

mapping_quality NARROW_MATCH -> CLOSE_MATCH, predicate skos:narrowMatch -> skos:closeMatch. narrowMatch asserts this record is *narrower in meaning* than CHEBI:37585 ('sodium dihydrogenphosphate') — a subsumption ChEBI itself denies: it files hydrates under CHEBI:35505 'hydrate', never under the anhydrous compound, which is not an ancestor even transitively. A hydrate is a distinct substance containing the anhydrous form, not a specialization of it. closeMatch claims similarity without subsumption. The ontology_id and the record's own identifier are unchanged.

A hydrate is a distinct substance containing the anhydrous form, not a specialization of it. closeMatch claims similarity without subsumption. The ontology_id and the record's own identifier are unchanged.

mapping_quality NARROW_MATCH -> CLOSE_MATCH, predicate skos:narrowMatch -> skos:closeMatch. narrowMatch asserts this record is *narrower in meaning* than CHEBI:30812 ('iron dichloride') — a subsumption ChEBI itself denies: it files hydrates under CHEBI:35505 'hydrate', never under the anhydrous compound, which is not an ancestor even transitively. A hydrate is a distinct substance containing the anhydrous form, not a specialization of it. closeMatch claims similarity without subsumption. The ontology_id and the record's own identifier are unchanged.

A hydrate is a distinct substance containing the anhydrous form, not a specialization of it. closeMatch claims similarity without subsumption. The ontology_id and the record's own identifier are unchanged.

identifier CHEBI:35696 -> kgmicrobe.compound:cocl2_x_2_h2o; mapping_quality EXACT_MATCH -> NARROW_MATCH. The record is a hydrate of CHEBI:35696 ('cobalt dichloride') and was sharing that term's identifier — the identity collapse MAPPING_SEMANTICS §3 forbids, which made a distinct substance indistinguishable from its anhydrous parent downstream. molecular_formula '2Cl.Co' -> '2Cl.Co.2H2O'. The recorded value described the anhydrous salt while the label names a hydrate, understating the mass by 18 g/mol per water. Corrected because the label states 2 water(s) of hydration, and the recorded formula was byte-identical to the anhydrous parent CHEBI:35696's ChEBI formula ('2Cl.Co') — the mark of a value inherited from the parent rather than measured for this record. Water appended in ChEBI's own dot-separated notation.

mapping_quality NARROW_MATCH -> CLOSE_MATCH, predicate skos:narrowMatch -> skos:closeMatch. narrowMatch asserts this record is *narrower in meaning* than CHEBI:35696 ('cobalt dichloride') — a subsumption ChEBI itself denies: it files hydrates under CHEBI:35505 'hydrate', never under the anhydrous compound, which is not an ancestor even transitively. A hydrate is a distinct substance containing the anhydrous form, not a specialization of it. closeMatch claims similarity without subsumption. The ontology_id and the record's own identifier are unchanged.

MediaDive578 and five current source recipes name CoCl2·2H2O; publisher-deposited primary abstract reports single-crystal CoCl2·2H2O. CHEBI35696 is the closest verified water-free parent; use NARROW_MATCH/broadMatch and retain exact local identity. Current2Cl.Co.2H2O matches the source-defined stoichiometry. Dry structure fields were removed in7b and remain absent. Computed PubChem is corroboration, not the sole experimental proof. evidence.notes: [HISTORICAL — superseded by the #321 re-grade below: this record is a hydrate of CHEBI:37585, not an exact match to it] Imported from CultureMech pipeline, quality=DIRECT_MATCH

identifier CHEBI:37585 -> kgmicrobe.compound:nah2po4_x_2_h2o; mapping_quality SYNONYM_MATCH -> NARROW_MATCH. The record is a hydrate of CHEBI:37585 ('sodium dihydrogenphosphate') and was sharing that term's identifier — the identity collapse MAPPING_SEMANTICS §3 forbids, which made a distinct substance indistinguishable from its anhydrous parent downstream. ChEBI has no term for this hydrate and the record carries no verified CAS, so steps 1 and 2 are unavailable and step 3 applies.

molecular_formula 'H2O4P.Na' -> 'H2O4P.Na.2H2O'. The recorded value described the anhydrous salt while the label names a hydrate, understating the mass by 18 g/mol per water. Corrected because the label states 2 water(s) of hydration, and the recorded formula was byte-identical to the anhydrous parent CHEBI:37585's ChEBI formula ('H2O4P.Na') — the mark of a value inherited from the parent rather than measured for this record. Water appended in ChEBI's own dot-separated notation.

mapping_quality NARROW_MATCH -> CLOSE_MATCH, predicate skos:narrowMatch -> skos:closeMatch. narrowMatch asserts this record is *narrower in meaning* than CHEBI:37585 ('sodium dihydrogenphosphate') — a subsumption ChEBI itself denies: it files hydrates under CHEBI:35505 'hydrate', never under the anhydrous compound, which is not an ancestor even transitively. A hydrate is a distinct substance containing the anhydrous form, not a specialization of it. closeMatch claims similarity without subsumption. The ontology_id and the record's own identifier are unchanged.
